title: The real Flannan interior
setting: Eilean Mor, Flannan Isles; game date 3 January 1901
scope: Local study references. Photographs and scans are retained unchanged; no generated concepts are included.
dateBoundary: No domestic photograph in this pack is verified as a photograph of the rooms in 1901. The room photographs depict later occupation; lasting architectural features can guide the reconstruction, while movable furnishings, paint and room assignments need separate evidence.

images.title: Living and dining room
images.reportedAttribution: Ron Ireland is credited for the related interior photographs on Keith McCloskey's author page. The original image-to-image match remains unverified because that site did not resolve during retrieval.
images.dateNote: The download mirror captions this view circa 1971. McCloskey's indexed page dates its corresponding room views to the 1960s. The retained filename follows that earlier lead and does not establish the date.
images.observed: Deep splayed window recesses, a boarded ceiling and a communal table in a plain working room.
images.use: Study the recess depth, wall mass, ceiling construction and economical furniture arrangement. Confirm geometry against original domestic plans before changing the layout.
images.exclude: Glass-block glazing, radio, electric fittings and later upholstered chairs. The weathered finish is not a reference for a recently built 1901 station.
images.confidence: Photograph identified as Flannan interior by the mirror; exact date, photographer match and continuity of each fitting are not independently established.

images.title: Room viewed from the kitchen
images.reportedAttribution: Related interior views credited to Ron Ireland on Keith McCloskey's indexed page; original pixel match pending.
images.dateNote: Mirror: circa 1971. Indexed author caption: 1960s, looking out from the kitchen. Neither date has been confirmed from an original negative or archive record.
images.observed: A second view of the table, chairs, thick walls and deep window reveals.
images.use: Cross-check the first photograph's room proportions and the relationship between doorways and windows. The precise kitchen-to-room assignment still needs the domestic drawings.
images.exclude: Later glass blocks, electrical equipment and modern upholstery.
images.confidence: Later photographic evidence, not a measured 1901 plan.

images.title: Timber-panelled interior
images.reportedAttribution: Photographer not stated alongside this image on the download page.
images.dateNote: The room location and survival of the panelling from 1901 are not established. This is a small 280-pixel-wide reproduction, useful for broad arrangement rather than joinery detail.
images.observed: Vertical timber panelling, a wall clock, hanging cloth, rugs and an adjoining room with a sash window.
images.use: Study the practical scale and use of timber finishes. Treat the blue-grey lower panels, brown stain, rugs and exact clock as later evidence until corroborated.
images.exclude: Electrical light fittings and modern upholstered seating.
images.confidence: Mirror identifies a Flannan interior during late manned service; exact room, photographer and earlier finish history unresolved.

images.title: Table at a sash window
images.reportedAttribution: Photographer not stated alongside this image on the download page.
images.dateNote: Small reproduction. It establishes the photographed later arrangement, not the position of a table in 1901.
images.observed: A deep window surround with timber lining, a closely placed table and ordinary cups and utensils.
images.use: Study the relationship of daylight, the recess and furniture at human scale. Period cups and utensils need their own dated object references.
images.exclude: Radio, electric kettle and modern packaged food. Do not reproduce the table setting as evidence of the 1900 disappearance.
images.confidence: Later station photograph identified by the mirror; original date and photographer pending.

images.title: Original lantern — Sheet 1
images.reportedAttribution: Scanned engineering sheet headed Northern Lights / Flannan Isles Lighthouse Lantern. Archive accession for this reproduction has not been matched.
images.dateNote: Use the visible original title and drawn details. The mirror's date and an exact catalogue match remain to be checked against the archive master.
images.observed: Lantern elevation and circular plan, diagonal glazing, lower wall panels and portholes, supports and roof form.
images.use: Guide the lantern's structural arrangement; read the scale and annotations from an archive-quality copy before taking dimensions.
images.exclude: This is a lantern drawing, not the kitchen, bedroom or keeper's-house floor plan.
images.confidence: Original-design drawing reproduced by a secondary site; archive identity pending.

images.title: Original lantern — Sheet 4 details
images.reportedAttribution: Engineering sheet headed Flannan Isles Lighthouse, Sheet No. 4. Archive accession for this reproduction has not been matched.
images.dateNote: Small text is partly legible; do not guess unreadable specifications or treat a design sheet as proof that every part was installed exactly as drawn.
images.observed: Glazing-bar and sash details, door handrails, iron bolts and structural connections.
images.use: Replace generic lantern fittings with the visible designed profiles and construction relationships. Dimensions and unclear labels await an archive master.
images.confidence: Original-design detail drawing reproduced by a secondary site; archive identity pending.

images.title: The original 1899 optic
images.reportedAttribution: Museum of Scottish Lighthouses, reproduced by the US Lighthouse Society. Retained from the project's earlier research pack.
images.dateNote: The date describes the apparatus, not the photograph. Cross-check museum object SLM.1997.9316 for surviving original prism material.
images.observed: Large Henry-Lepaute hyper-radial bivalve optic, paired bullseyes and prism assembly.
images.use: Controlling reference for the original optic's scale, paired bullseyes and prism arrangement.
images.exclude: The smaller replacement optic installed around automation is unsuitable for the 1901 scene. Details outside the photograph remain reconstructed.
images.confidence: Museum-attributed original apparatus photograph with supporting museum object record.

sources.title: Northern Lighthouse Board — 1900/1901 reports
sources.role: Period evidence for the kitchen fireplace, rooms and empty beds, cleaned pots and pans, clocks, slate and working records. These reports do not establish a detailed furniture inventory or a visual layout.

sources.title: Historic Environment Scotland — listed-building record
sources.role: Describes the serpentine cast-iron staircase, timber handrail, timber deck on iron girders and moulded portholes. Later survey: distinguish original structure from recorded modern alterations.

sources.title: HES/Trove — original kitchen, bedroom and coal-cellar drawing
sources.role: DP 038541 / DC 8666B / C/32/9, dated 16 May 1896 in the catalogue. Full drawing not obtained: viewer presents an automated access check. Exact house layout remains unresolved.

sources.title: HES/Trove — station archive catalogue
sources.role: Domestic sheets DC 8665 and DC 8666A/B; lantern and lightroom series DC 8667–8673. Catalogue pointers are not substitutes for inspecting the original drawings.

sources.title: Keith McCloskey — interior photographs credited to Ron Ireland
sources.role: Search-indexed captions identify two real interior views and credit Ron Ireland, dating them to the 1960s. Live site did not resolve. The claim that everything except chairs was unchanged is not adopted as proof of 1901 accuracy.

sources.title: 9001.lt — photographic and drawing mirror
sources.role: Download source for four interior photographs and two original lantern drawing scans. Secondary compilation; photograph dates and original archive/photographer identities are not fully documented.

sources.title: Museum of Scottish Lighthouses — surviving 1899 prism
sources.role: Object SLM.1997.9316: original hyper-radial prism material, confirming the original apparatus reference.

sources.title: US Lighthouse Society — hyper-radial lenses
sources.role: Museum-attributed photograph and history of the original 1899 Henry-Lepaute bivalve optic.

sources.title: Northern Lighthouse Board — station history
sources.role: Station first lit in 1899; automated in 1971. The domestic photo set is decades later than the game date.
